result: CIP demonstrated nanomolar-range in vitro efficacy against Babesia species, with IC50 values of 20.2 ± 1.4 nM for B. bovis and 69.4 ± 2.2 nM for B. gibsoni. These values indicate potent antiparasitic activity in vitro.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirmed this finding, with one stating 'In vitro growth assays were used to establish that cipargamin is effective against Babesia bovis and Babesia gibsoni' and another noting the authors 'proved the efficacy of CIP on babesia in the nanomolar range.' The editor also confirmed 'the evidence is solid with the methods, data, and analyses broadly supporting the claims.'

result: CIP significantly inhibited B. microti growth in vivo in BALB/c mice, achieving peak parasitemia of 1.06 ± 0.20% compared to 38.55 ± 4.32% in vehicle controls, with efficacy comparable to the standard atovaquone plus azithromycin combination. CIP treatment also prevented anemia development as measured by hematocrit levels.
evaluation: A reviewer explicitly stated 'Infection of mice with Babesia microti demonstrated that cipargamin is as effective as the combination of atovaquone plus azithromycin.' Another reviewer noted 'the conclusions drawn by the authors are well justified by the data presented,' and the editor confirmed 'the evidence is solid.'

result: CIP protected mice from lethal B. rodhaini infection, achieving a 66.67% survival rate compared to 0% in control groups. CIP treatment prevented parasitemia emergence for 8 days, though parasites recurred at 12 DPI before being cleared by 18 DPI.
evaluation: A reviewer explicitly affirmed this result, stating 'Cipargamin protected mice from lethal infection with Babesia rodhaini.' The comprehensive nature of the study was praised by another reviewer who noted 'All the experiments performed were carried out methodically and logically.'

result: Resistance selection experiments identified two mutations in BgATP4 at position L921 (L921V and L921I) that conferred 6.1-fold and 12.8-fold reduced sensitivity to CIP, respectively. These mutations were confirmed by Sanger sequencing and NGS with >99.9% purity.
evaluation: A reviewer explicitly validated this finding: 'Mutations that confer resistance to cipargamin were identified in the gene encoding ATP4, a P-type Na ATPase that is found in other apicomplexan parasites, thereby validating ATP4 as the target of cipargamin.' Another reviewer noted 'In silico analyses revealed the drug resistance mechanism through a single amino acid mutation at amino acid position 921 on the ATP4 gene of babesia.'

result: The L921V and L921I mutations reduced CIP inhibition of BgATP4-associated ATPase activity by 1.3-fold and 2.4-fold, respectively. The mutant strains showed reduced basal ATPase activity and higher IC50 values for CIP inhibition of ATPase activity, correlating with their resistance to CIP-mediated growth inhibition.
evaluation: While not explicitly discussed in detail by reviewers, this mechanistic data supporting the resistance findings was implicitly accepted as part of the comprehensive study. One reviewer stated 'the conclusions drawn by the authors are well justified by the data presented,' and the editor confirmed 'the evidence is solid with the methods, data, and analyses broadly supporting the claims.'

result: CIP treatment caused parasite swelling, cytoplasmic vacuolization, increased intracellular Na+ concentration, and cytosolic alkalinization in wild-type B. gibsoni. These effects were attenuated in resistant mutant strains, supporting the mechanism that internal alkalinization and Na+ absorption are key factors in parasite death.
evaluation: These mechanistic findings were implicitly accepted as part of the comprehensive study praised by reviewers. One reviewer noted 'The authors have carried out a comprehensive study. All the experiments performed were carried out methodically and logically.' The editor confirmed 'the evidence is solid with the methods, data, and analyses broadly supporting the claims.'

result: Molecular docking studies revealed that CIP binds near L921 in BgATP4, with predicted binding affinities of −6.43, −6.40, and −6.26 kcal/mol for wild-type, L921V, and L921I variants, respectively. The L921I mutation created a steric clash reducing binding affinity more than L921V.
evaluation: While not explicitly discussed by reviewers, this computational work supporting the resistance mechanism was implicitly accepted. One reviewer noted 'In silico analyses revealed the drug resistance mechanism,' and the editor stated the study has 'practical and theoretical implications for drug discovery, particularly in the context of repurposing cipargamin.'

result: CIP-resistant strains showed no significant cross-resistance to atovaquone or tafenoquine, with less than onefold change in IC50 values for both drugs across wild-type and mutant strains.
evaluation: This finding was implicitly accepted as part of the comprehensive study. The lack of cross-resistance is important for combination therapy strategies, which reviewers acknowledged when discussing the combination treatment results. The editor confirmed 'the evidence is solid.'

result: Combination therapy of CIP plus tafenoquine effectively eliminated B. microti infection in immunocompromised SCID mice with no relapse, achieving complete parasite clearance by 6 DPI with no detectable parasite DNA by qPCR at 90 DPI. In contrast, CIP monotherapy resulted in relapse despite initial clearance.
evaluation: A reviewer explicitly affirmed this key finding: 'A 7-day treatment of cipagarmin, when combined with a single dose of tafenoquine, was sufficient to eradicate Babesia microti in a mouse model of severe babesiosis caused by a lack of adaptive immunity.' The editor confirmed this represents 'valuable findings with practical and theoretical implications for drug discovery.'

result: CIP demonstrated favorable safety profiles with CC50 values of 38.7 ± 2.0 μM for MDCK cells and 70.8 ± 4.9 μM for HFFs, yielding selectivity indices greater than 500. CIP also showed minimal hemolytic activity at 100 μM (0.11 ± 0.03%).
evaluation: While not explicitly discussed by reviewers, these safety data were implicitly accepted as part of the comprehensive study. The editor noted the study presents 'valuable findings with practical and theoretical implications for drug discovery,' which encompasses safety considerations.

result: Sequence analysis showed B. gibsoni ATP4 shares 29.75% identity with human ATP4, 49.40% with P. falciparum ATP4, 49.67% with T. gondii ATP4, 62.21% with B. bovis ATP4, and 52.47% with B. microti ATP4.
evaluation: This comparative sequence analysis was implicitly accepted as supporting data. The low homology with human ATP4 is relevant to the drug's selectivity, which reviewers acknowledged when accepting the overall safety and efficacy profile.

result: The growth and generation rates of CIP-resistant mutant strains were comparable to wild-type strains, indicating that resistance mutations do not impose significant fitness costs.
evaluation: While not explicitly discussed by reviewers, this observation was implicitly accepted as part of the resistance characterization. Reviewers praised the comprehensive nature of the study without raising concerns about this claim.
